CHIEF COMPLAINT
Severe right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 39-year-old female who sustained a right upper arm injury while playing volleyball yesterday at approximately 7 PM. She was spiking the ball when an opponent kicked her legs out from under her as she was going up, causing her to fall and land on her right shoulder. Time of injury was approximately 18 hours prior to this visit. She describes the pain as 9 out of 10 in severity. She has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours but reports it is not helping. She denies using ice. X-ray imaging reveals a proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies numbness or tingling in the right arm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones.
Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen every 6 hours.
Pepcid.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays recreational volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Exam otherwise normal. Able to straighten elbow without moving shoulder. Swelling and erythema noted over right shoulder. Tenderness over right shoulder. Normal pulses. No numbness or tingling in right arm.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm shows proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture. Plan for immobilization with long arm cast and sling. Follow-up in 2 weeks to assess bone realignment; surgery may be considered if bones have not realigned. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain, 20 tablets dispensed.
